key_insight: CatDiT is a unified diffusion-transformer framework that inverse-designs heterogeneous catalysts by jointly controlling adsorbate type, binding energy, and catalyst class in a compressed latent space.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable route to rapidly screen and generate candidate catalysts for reaction-specific targets, reducing the trial-and-error burden in materials discovery.
method: Learns compressed latent representations of catalyst structures for efficient training and fast sampling.
Uses a diffusion transformer to generate valid, novel catalysts across intermetallic alloys and oxide surfaces.
Supports multi-conditional generation on discrete and continuous properties for targeted inverse design.
evidence_signal: For nitrogen reduction reaction design, the model produced 28 DFT-relaxed alloy candidates within the target activity window and above the pure-metal *N-*H scaling line, achieving about 1.5× enrichment over the source distribution.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the latent training data, and DFT relaxation is still required to verify generated candidates.
paper_title: Catalyst Diffusion Transformer: Generative Inverse Design of Heterogeneous Catalysts
